newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's north sees better barley, rape yields.
newsitem.headline: Germany's north sees better barley, rape yields.

text.p: Farmers in Germany's most northerly state of Schleswig-Holstein are reporting higher winter barley and rapeseed yields from the current 1997 harvest, the regional chamber of agriculture said.
Farmers had brought in more than 90 percent of barley and between 10 and 20 percent of the rape harvest amid sunny weather, following frequent rainfall in July.
Rye, winter wheat and spring barley crops need another fortnight to mature.
Winter barley yields were in a 6.00-10.00 tonne per hectare (tph) range compared with 6.82 tph last year in Schleswig-Holstein and the 5.61 tph German national barley yield average for 1996.
It was hoped the average could be above 7.00 tph this year, a spokesman for the chamber said.
The winter barley area this year is 69,949 hectares, down from 72,066 ha last year when the state harvested 491,300 tonnes.
The rapeseed area this year is up at 82,022 ha from 78,202 ha in 1996 when the state harvested 237,000 tonnes.
Farmers were aiming to exceed the 3.03 tph yield achieved in 1996, with early samples at 4.00 tph, but further progress depended on the weather.
Rapeseed moisture of 10-14 percent compared with a standard nine percent and this meant the seed needed drying.
Ex-harvest rapeseeed prices were between 400 and 420 marks a tonne.
Barley moisture was up to 19 percent and had to be dried down to 15 percent.
Specific weights were between 62 and 70 kilos per hectolitre, which the chamber called satisfactory.
